title: Throwing Custom Errors
objective: Signal your own error condition with throw, and catch it with catch (err).

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge chapter; not aligned to a specific book chapter. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Not every error comes from JavaScript itself — sometimes your own code needs to refuse to continue because a value doesn't make sense, like a negative price or a missing required field. The throw statement lets you raise your own error on purpose: throw new Error("message").

new Error("message") creates an Error object carrying that text. Throwing it immediately stops the current function — just like a built-in error would — and hands control to the nearest catch block, if one is wrapping the call.

Inside a catch (err) block, err.message holds the exact text you passed to new Error(...). This lets the code that catches the error report something specific and useful, instead of a generic failure.
explanation.rule: throw new Error("message") raises your own error; catch (err) receives it, with err.message holding the text you threw.

examples.title: Refusing an Invalid Value
examples.note: setVolume(150) throws before returning anything. The catch block receives that error and reads its message.

checks.question: throw new Error("Out of range") is caught by catch (err). What does err.message equal?

feedback.correct: Correct — err.message holds exactly the text passed to new Error(...).
feedback.incorrect: err.message is the text you passed to new Error(...) when you threw it — here, "Out of range".

assignment.title: Validated Deposit
assignment.brief: Write deposit(amount) that throws new Error('Deposit must be positive.') if amount is 0 or negative, otherwise returns amount. Then write tryDeposit(amount) that calls deposit(amount) in a try block, returning the result on success or the caught error's message on failure.
requirements: Define deposit(amount) that throws for amount <= 0, otherwise returns amount.
Define tryDeposit(amount) that calls deposit(amount) inside try/catch.
On success, tryDeposit returns deposit's return value.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: tryDeposit(50) returns 50; tryDeposit(-10) returns the thrown error's message

hints: deposit(amount) should throw new Error('Deposit must be positive.') when amount is 0 or negative.
tryDeposit wraps the deposit(amount) call in try, and returns whatever it returns on success.
In the catch block, return err.message rather than the whole error object.
tryDeposit(50) should return 50; tryDeposit(-10) should return the string 'Deposit must be positive.'
